title: Four series: a geometric sum, the nth term test, the integral test and a p-series

stimulus.title: Four series
stimulus.html:
The four series below are used in parts (a) through (d). No calculator is allowed.

The series for each part (kk is a positive constant)
PartSeries
(a)∑n=2∞3(−25)n\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} 3\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right)^n
(b)∑n=1∞n23n2+1\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n^2}{3n^2 + 1}
(c)∑n=1∞ne−n2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} ne^{-n^2}
(d)∑n=1∞nnk\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\sqrt{n}}{n^{k}}

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The series in part (a) is geometric. Explain why it converges, and find its sum.

rubric.point: Ratio <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = -\frac{2}{5}</annotation></semantics></math> and convergence because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|r| < 1</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|-\frac{2}{5}\right| = \frac{2}{5} < 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the series converges

rubric.point: Sum <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>35</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{12}{35}</annotation></semantics></math>, from the first term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{12}{25}</annotation></semantics></math> (the term at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n = 2</annotation></semantics></math>) over <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - r</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: not earned for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{1 + 2/5} = \frac{15}{7}</annotation></semantics></math>, the sum from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The series is geometric with ratio <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = -\frac{2}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|r| = \frac{2}{5} < 1</annotation></semantics></math>, it converges. Its first term, at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 \cdot \frac{4}{25} = \frac{12}{25}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the sum is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{12/25}{1 - \left(-\frac{2}{5}\right)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{12/25}{7/5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>35</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{12}{35}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that the series in part (b) diverges.

rubric.point: Limit of the terms: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{n^2}{3n^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: dividing the top and bottom by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n^2</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Conclusion: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the series diverges by the nth term test
accept: not earned for \"the terms diverge\" or \"the series converges to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>\"

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{n^2}{3n^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{3 + 1/n^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since this limit is not 0, the series <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{n^2}{3n^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> diverges by the nth term test.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the integral test to determine whether the series in part (c) converges or diverges. Show that the conditions for the test are met.

rubric.point: Conditions: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = xe^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> is positive, continuous and decreasing for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ge 1</annotation></semantics></math>, with decreasing shown, for example <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= e^{-x^2}(1 - 2x^2) < 0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ge 1</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: decreasing justified by the sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Improper integral in limit notation, evaluated: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b \to \infty} \int_1^{b} xe^{-x^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{b \to \infty} \left(\frac{1}{2e} - \frac{1}{2}e^{-b^2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2e}</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: the antiderivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}e^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> with the limit kept to the end

not earned with arithmetic on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, such as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}e^{-\infty^2}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Conclusion: the integral converges, so the series converges by the integral test
accept: not earned for \"the series converges to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2e}</annotation></semantics></math>\"

parts.sample: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = xe^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ge 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is positive and continuous, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= e^{-x^2} - 2x^2e^{-x^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= e^{-x^2}(1 - 2x^2) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing. Then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^{\infty} xe^{-x^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">[</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">]</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{b \to \infty} \Big[-\frac{1}{2}e^{-x^2}\Big]_1^{b}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{b \to \infty} \left(-\frac{1}{2}e^{-b^2} + \frac{1}{2e}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2e}</annotation></semantics></math>. The improper integral converges, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mi>n</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} ne^{-n^2}</annotation></semantics></math> converges by the integral test.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find all values of kk for which the series in part (d) converges. Justify your answer.

rubric.point: Rewrite as a <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-series: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mi>n</mi></msqrt><msup><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{n}}{n^{k}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{n^{k - 1/2}}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p = k - \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n^{1/2 - k}</annotation></semantics></math> identified as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{n^p}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p = k - \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Answer <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>></mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k > \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, because a <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-series converges exactly when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p > 1</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: not earned for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k \ge \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k = \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> the series is harmonic and diverges

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mi>n</mi></msqrt><msup><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{n}}{n^{k}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{n^{k - 1/2}}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the series is a <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-series with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p = k - \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. A <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-series converges exactly when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p > 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the series converges for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k - \frac{1}{2} > 1</annotation></semantics></math>, that is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>></mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k > \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. (At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k = \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> it is the harmonic series, which diverges.)
